study.title: Optimizing Input Selection for Cardiac Model Training and Inference: An Efficient 3D Convolutional Neural Networks-Based Approach to Automate Coronary Angiogram Video Selection

imaging.modality_detail: Invasive X-ray coronary angiogram cine video clips

public_dataset_used.detail: Private Mayo Clinic data (Minnesota, Florida, Arizona); development set 209 patients/232 exams/1037 videos; independent set 2725 patients/3208 exams/20,388 videos

task.task_description: Binary clip-level quality classification (satisfactory vs unsatisfactory) of coronary angiogram video clips to automate input selection for downstream ML models
task.clinical_application: Automated quality control / input selection of coronary angiogram videos for ML model training and pre-inference screening

temporal_evidence.quote: 2D models handle each frame independently and merge the results, which may lead to inefficiencies, whereas 3D models process multiple frames in sequence, directly yielding predictions.

evaluation.external_validation_detail: Independent dataset of 3208 examinations / 20,388 videos from the same 3 Mayo Clinic sites; authors state no external validation was performed

other_limitations: No direct comparison of downstream models trained on manually vs automatically curated datasets
No universal standard for classifying images as unsatisfactory (e.g., CABG native vessels, foreign objects)
Performance decline on independent dataset (precision 0.87 to 0.63)
future_work: Compare downstream models trained on manually curated vs automatically selected datasets
Evaluate combined generalizability of selection and downstream models on external datasets
Inter-institutional collaborations to gather images from varied regions and populations
